topics.title: JMW: The Hair Dryer in Every Korean Salon, and the Marketing Word Hiding What It Actually Did
topics.notes: REPRESENTATIVE PROPOSED 2026-08-08. Premise to correct, not repeat: the rep (and every English listing) says JMW makes aircraft motors. It does not. | VERIFIED: founded 2004, CEO 강민웅, 주식회사 제이엠더블유. Korean R&D and domestic production of professional hair devices. | VERIFIED: first in Korea to put a BLDC motor in a hair dryer -- this part is real and did change the category. 1M cumulative BLDC dryer units by 2017. 8 consecutive years #1 in 올해의 브랜드 대상 hair dryer category (as of 2025). | THE ANGLE: 항공모터 (aircraft motor) is a MARKETING TERM, now a whole product category on Danawa that competitors (밀다 etc.) also use. Real aircraft use engines; BLDC motors appear in RC aircraft, helicopters and drones. Korean consumers already question it -- Clien thread 10982168 titled "JMW드라이기의 BLDC 모터는 항공모터??". Korean commenters compare it to 항공냄비 aluminium cookware. | So the thesis is the third counter-example in a row after 오뚜기 (did not export) and 풀무원 (bought American brands): JMW built a genuinely good thing and then buried it under a word that is not true. The real story is domestic BLDC engineering and salon-grade durability. | COVERAGE GATE looks CLEAN: English web has Amazon/retailer listings and a Canadian distributor site repeating "aircraft motor" verbatim. No English editorial or journalistic examination found. That is the gap. | SECTION FIT: would be the first appliance/hardware manufacturer in the business section, which is currently food (samyang/ottogi/pulmuone), beauty (cosmax/apr-medicube) and platforms (coupang/musinsa/toss/iconix). | STILL TO VERIFY BEFORE DRAFTING: revenue and salon share (not public in search; check 나이스평가정보 / DART if they file), export markets, employee count, patent filings (a US patent 8922082 "BLDC motor for a hairdryer" surfaced -- confirm assignee), and whether JMW has ever claimed aerospace supply itself vs distributors adding it. | IMAGE NOTE: 0차 rule applies -- jmwkorea.com serves a self-signed cert so WebFetch fails; use a browser UA via curl, or jmwmall.co.kr / jmwprofessional.com.
